title: Canonical etale module functors of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the small etale structure sheaves and their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an etale scheme $V\to Y$, let $\mathcal A(f,V)$ have objects etale scheme charts $T\to X$ together with a scheme map $a:T\to V$ over $Y$, and morphisms the commuting chart maps over $X$ and $V$. For a module $F$ on $X$, its chart diagram on $\mathcal A(f,V)^{op}$ has value $F(T)$, regarded as a $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-module via $a^\sharp$, and has the restriction maps of $F$. Define the canonical module direct image $f_*$ by the limit universal property $(f_*F)(V)=\lim_{\mathcal A(f,V)^{op}}F(T)$, with its specified chart projections. For maps of test schemes and module morphisms the projections commute with the same restrictions and module maps. This property determines the direct-image functor up to unique natural isomorphism preserving every projection. Define the tensor pullback $f^*$, namely $\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}(-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], by its adjunction to this specified $f_*$. Retain its unit $\eta$. For $m\in G(V)$, a chart $(T,a)$, and $b\in\mathcal O_X(T)$, the local tensor $b\otimes m$ is $b\,\pi_{T,a}(\eta_G(m))$ in $(f^*G)(T)$. Limits and adjoints are taken by their universal properties, without choosing arbitrary functors or maps.

from.place: Canonical arbitrary-module direct images and tensor pullbacks used by the section-algebra and adjunction-map etale comparison in the polarized descent input.

lean.note: The chart category, regular-function scalar maps and chart diagram have real data. The direct-image model includes the complete section-limit universal property and its naturality in both arguments; moduleDirectImageModel_unique records uniqueness by every chart projection. Selection uses this normalized universal property, the exception expressly allowed by AGENTS.md section 5, and tensor pullback is the left adjoint retaining its unit. The named supporting theorems have source and complete proof docstrings; none of the definitions has a sorry body. No independent equality between site and coefficient universes is imposed.
